tracks.title: Two Exits Past Ardmore
tracks.subject: waiting in a truck outside a diner on I-35
tracks.caption: Stadium country with a modern pop mix. Pedal steel used as a held texture rather than a solo, clean Telecaster on muted downstrokes, upright-feeling bass with a tight modern sub, real drum kit close-miked with room on the snare only. Dry conversational female lead, doubled only on the hook, no reverb wash. 88 BPM, D major. Patient, stubborn, unsentimental. No pop, no synth, no gang vocals, no key change.

tracks.title: Aunt Rose Won't Sit Down
tracks.subject: an aunt who dances through an entire wedding reception
tracks.caption: Afro house with a sung pop topline. Rolling log drum and conga polyrhythm carrying the groove, offbeat sub-bass, long slow-filtered pad builds, shakers panned wide, a single dry rim click marking the bar. Warm female lead with a chanted group answer, call and response, light saturation on the stack. 122 BPM, A minor. Warm, relentless, celebratory without being triumphant. No trap hats, no EDM riser, no supersaw, no drop.

tracks.title: Dead Mall Security
tracks.subject: a night security guard in a mall with no tenants
tracks.caption: Rage rap. Bitcrushed detuned lead synth carrying the whole melody, 808 driven into clipping on purpose, sparse hi-hats with long gaps, no snare fills, deliberate mp3 artifacting on the tails. Fast deadpan male rap, flat affect, screamed ad-libs mixed as loud as the lead vocal, hard autotune used texturally on the hook only. 162 BPM, F sharp minor. Flat, dissociated, bored rather than angry. No trap hi-hat rolls, no clean 808 slides, no boom bap, no melodic trap.

[Hook - screamed ad-libs layered]

Fountain's dry, they filled it with those white rocks
Kid on a scooter doing laps around the pretzel place
I'd tell him to slow down but I'd have to stand up

[Hook - screamed ad-libs layered]
Nothing in the bag, nothing in the bag
Walk it to the car like it's expensive
Nothing in the bag

[Outro - 808 clipping]
[Song ends abruptly]

tracks.title: Whose Name Is On The Gas
tracks.subject: sorting out a utility bill after someone moves out
tracks.caption: Three-step, the spacious swung successor to 2-step. Shuffled kick with a wide swing, dubby minor chord stabs left to decay into silence, deep round sub, one closed hat and nothing else, deliberate negative space where a fill would be. Half-spoken male lead recorded close and left unprocessed, one whispered double on the hook. 132 BPM, C minor. Numb, practical, quietly funny. No 2-step garage skippers, no vocal chops, no build, no drop.

tracks.title: Ring Light, Four Dollars
tracks.subject: filming a sponsored post while broke
tracks.caption: Post-hyperpop indie, digital maximalism. Clipped drums with the transients squared off, pitched vocal stacks used as pads, granular chops of the lead vocal as a melodic instrument, bass distorted until it reads as a guitar, deliberate mp3 artifacting left audible on the pre-chorus. Pitched-up layered female lead answered by one completely dry unprocessed take. 145 BPM, E minor. Bright, panicked, forced cheerfulness. No clean mastering, no tropical house, no sad-girl piano, no four on the floor.

[Verse 1]

Caption says consistency, my hands are shaking from the coffee
Brand paid in product, product is a tub
Tub is on the shelf behind me in every single video

[Chorus]
Ring light on, four dollars in
Ring light on, four dollars in

One of them was my landlord
He hearted it

[Song ends abruptly]

Live kendang played with audible ghost notes and a proper kendang break filling into every chorus, bamboo suling weaving a counter-melody rather than soloing, synth brass stabs, sub-bass under the traditional pattern.
